Pre-selector opportunistic baseline is documented: activation 37260572520 (logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md) objective 'came from the queued receipt item rather than a frontier cell' and its process-level delta was recorded UNVERIFIED (state/LEARNING_STATE.md line 51).
unverified: No controlled counterfactual exists: opportunistic selection cannot be re-run to measure what it would have produced, so aggregate causal superiority of frontier-first selection is not proven; the 'before' evidence is a small number of documented activations (principally 37260572520).
The selectivity advantage is evidenced qualitatively (distinct cells closed, decisive verdicts, no equivalent retests, auditable selection) rather than by a counted duplicate-retest baseline.

Closest near-duplicate pair: momentum (long previous return) and mean-reversion (short previous return) are sign-flips of the same autocorrelation bet tested as separate cells; they returned opposite decisive verdicts (reversal FALSIFIED, momentum SUPPORTED), so the pair was informative sign-identification rather than a redundant retest, but it tempers any claim of literally zero equivalent retests.
observed_effect: Concrete selector advantage demonstrated in SELECTIVITY and AUDITABILITY, bounded by an uncontrolled counterfactual. In the frontier-first period each activation selected a distinct unresolved frontier cell and closed it with a decisive, independently verified verdict with no equivalent retests (mean-reversion, cross-sectional relative strength, volatility targeting, momentum, longer-horizon momentum, cross-sectional momentum, 20-day breakout); the pre-selector period's documented activation (37260572520) produced no clean process delta precisely because its objective came from the queue rather than a frontier cell. The controller's explicit ordinal rank plus recorded selection_history make the choice reconstructable. Net: the frontier-first focused-task selector improves learning efficiency in the demonstrable senses (distinct decisive cells, no redundant re-tests, auditable selection) while a strict causal 'more information per activation' claim remains unresolved for lack of a controlled comparison.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection improves learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic queue-based task choice.
uncertainty_reduced: Reduced: established the selector is operative and produces distinct, decisive, independently-verified frontier cells with no equivalent retests, and that its selection is auditable (concrete selectivity advantage). Not fully resolved: aggregate causal superiority over opportunistic choice is uncontrolled (no counterfactual; small pre-period sample), and the closest near-duplicate (momentum vs mean-reversion sign-flip pair) shows the 'zero equivalent retests' phrasing needs qualification.
research_result: No new market research result (learning-process audit); research frontier unchanged. Process finding: the frontier-first focused-task selector is retained. It demonstrably yields distinct, decisive, independently-verified frontier cells with no equivalent retests and an auditable selection trail, versus a documented opportunistic baseline that failed to produce a clean process delta. The advantage is concrete in selectivity/auditability but not proven in aggregate causal terms.
next: At the next LEARNING_PROCESS activation, execute candidate task P-007 to convert this qualitative selectivity finding into a counted equivalent-retest and decisive-closure comparison across durable activation records.
